newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial shares slide on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial shares slide on profit-taking.

text.p: Zimbabwe's main industrial share index tumbled over 87 points on Friday on profit-taking on some key counters in a market seen soft for some weeks.
"The market continues to be weak...but today we saw quite a number of profit-takers at play and that's what drove some shares down," one broker said.
"I don't think it will be sustained but the outlook remains one of weakness because of the new issues," he said.
The brokers analysts say quite a "considerable number" of local investors have their money tied up in new issues, and are expecting little activity in the coming two or so weeks.

The industrial index dropped 87.04 points to 10,261.63, pushed lower by losses in some bluechips, including five-star hotel and supermarkets group Meikles, which traded 50 cents down at 2,350, and bankers Barclays, which lost 200 cents to 3,500.
Banking group FM regained the 250 cents it lost on Thursday to 5,000.
The industrial index lost 216.88 since Monday.
The secondary seven-share mining index gained 31.32 points on Friday -- and 37.14 points on the week -- to close at 999.06 following some 60-cent rise in nickel producer Bindura at 810.
